HPI:
   This is a 79 yo F h/o ILD (normal O2 sat at baseline), RA,  atrial
   flutter, CHF, pacemaker, dementia admitted for hypoxia. Per call-in to
   ED, the patient fell yesterday; X-ray pelvic and lower back
   unremarkable. Then this morning at 4am, was found to be 79% on RA,
   improved to mid-90's on NRB. Per [**Hospital 328**] Rehab, the patient was not in
   distress or tachypnic. The patient herself is unable to answer
   questions reliably but denies pain or CP.
   .
   In the ED: The patient arrived hypoxic to 84 on ra and 88 on 4 L NC, 94
   on NRB. The patient was not tachypnic or in distress. CXR showed
   pulmonary edema; PE demonstrated crackles [**1-2**] way up lung fields
   bilaterally. BNP elevated to 3284. Trop neg. EKG with old Vpaced at 70,
   neg Sgarbossa's critera. She was placed on Bipap 10/5, nitro gtt and
   lasix 20mg IV.  She put out 650ml. Cardiology was called for admission
   to the CCU but refused the admission as pt has hx ILD.
   Vitals on admission: temp97.1 HR72 Bp134/73 RR24 93%NRB
   Vitals on transfer: Vpaced 70's LBBB afebrile 155/76 18 94% on BiPAp
   Pt had ct of chest this afternoon, and plans to have and echo
   .H/O heart failure (CHF), Diastolic, Acute on Chronic
   Assessment:
   Pt has crackles half up bilaterally, sats 89-91% on 5liters
   Action:
   pt given lasix 80 po this am, also had chest ct this afternoon
   Response:
   Pt put  out 460 of urine from lasix
   Plan:
   Chest  ct done this afternoon showing interstitial lung disease r/t ra,
   they feel now this is more the issue then chf, it on ra med and
   steroids, will need echo done
   .H/O dementia (including Alzheimer's, Multi Infarct)
   Assessment:
   Pt still has periods of confusion,  but can be agitated and combative
   at time although I have had no issues this am, has poor shot term
   memory
   Action:
   Pt reoriented, pt oob to chair,
   Response:
   Did well with direction, keeping directions simple
   Plan:
   Using least restrictive measures, encourage as much independence as
   possible with in reason of illness,
   Would keep pt within view of nursing station,  side rails x4,
   Fall(s)
   Assessment:
   Pt at high risk for falls had fallen the day before her admission
   Action:
   Pt within view of  desk, bed in low position,  pt reoriented
   Response:
   Pt has  been manageable, today oob to chair x4 hrs did well, with
   assistance
   Plan:
   Pt will continue to have 4 side rails, bed low and locked, pt
   reoriented as needed

However, the second “conflict” merely repeats the same text, offering no real contradiction, which weakens the overall conflict quality. The overall reconciliation is realistic but the conflict creation is only partially effective.

   of decompensated CHF & exacerbation of her underlying COPD. Patient
   with remote history of PNA resulting in loss of lung tissue.

   bring in patient

   treat hypernatermia.

   currently -875 since midnight (goal is even). Recent cardiac echo
   showed good EF and function of her AVR, also mild pulmonary HTN.

   Continue to wean O2 as tolerated,goal O2 sat 88-92%. Monitor I/O; goal
   negative, complete infusion of D5W at 100 ml/hr for 700 ml. Continue
   neb treatments; alert pharmacy when family brings in symbacort from
   home for approval. Monitor afternoon electrolytes, due at 5 pm.

   Patient pleasant, and oriented to person, place & time, however she is
   unable to answer questions such as
what would you like to eat
what pills do you take at home
. No attempts OOB with family present
   throughout the afternoon. Moderate-poor appetite per patient.
   Action:
   Attempted to engage patient in easy conversation. Discussed with family
   & accepting MD team the family
s concerns about her returning to an
   independent living situation. Bed alarm maintained and call light
   available.

   Continues without any attempts OOB & remains oriented, although
   pleasantly quiet. MD will obtain PT consult when medically ready prior
   to discharge. [**Name6 (MD) **] need RN case manager to assist patient and family
   with discharge planning when appropriate.

   Continue bed alarms. PT consult and RN case management follow-up prior
